text: . Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav today inaugurated a national workshop in Panchkula to mark International Vulture Awareness Day.In his address, Shri Bhupender Yadav said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the government’s approach to environmental conservation is based on a holistic, ecosystem-oriented model rather than being limited to any specific species.He noted that India is actively working towards the conservation of various vulture species. He called for the creation of safe zones for vultures and the development of technical capabilities to aid in the conservation of these species in the wild.

. Wall Street ended higher yesterday, after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he would be inclined to support holding rates steady barring any surprises in upcoming inflation data. Among the major indices, the Nasdaq Composite surged 1.4 per cent the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.2 per cent, and the S&P 500 gained 1.1 per cent.On the economic front, the unemployment insurance weekly claims increased by 2,000 to 2 lakh six thousand in the week ending August 29, according to the data released by US Department of Labour.Market participants closely watch the upcoming nonfarm payrolls data to gauge the Federal Reserve’s next policy stance.

. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Luxembourg Xavier Bettel has arrived in New Delhi for his official visit. The Ministry of External Affairs said that Mr Bettle is scheduled to have a meeting with External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar in the National Capital today. In a social media post, MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the visit provides an opportunity to further strengthen the multifaceted relations between India and Luxembourg.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will share his thoughts with the people of the country and abroad in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani at 11 AM on Sunday. It will be the 137th episode of the monthly radio programme. The programme will be broadcast across the entire Akashvani and Doordarshan network, the AIR News website, and the Newsonair mobile app. It will also be live-streamed on the YouTube channels of AIR News, DD News, the PMO, and the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Akashvani will broadcast the programme in regional languages immediately after the Hindi broadcast.

. Iran’s top security official has announced that a new restricted zone will be declared outside the Strait of Hormuz in the coming days, and that any vessel entering the area without coordination with them will be placed on an Iranian sanctions list.Major General Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) said that the zone will begin from the US Navy’s blockade line and extend into parts of the Persian Gulf. Ships that move toward the strait from either side and enter this area will face sanctions, the Iranian State Media reported.Rezaei said that traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped sharply since Iran closed the waterway and that only seven to eight ships carrying essential goods for Iran are now transiting, compared with more than 100 ships before. Rezaei also claimed US vessels attempting to pass through the strait have been struck. He said Iran has refrained from sinking them because of the environmental risks posed by their oil cargo.

. Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan has urged young people to stay away from drugs and encourage their friends to say no to drugs.Addressing the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Geetanagar College in Guwahati today, he stressed that students must make responsible choices and safeguard their time, health and future. C P Radhakrishnan said India’s young population is its greatest strength and that the opportunities emerging in areas such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, space research and entrepreneurship can enable the youth to play a leading role in building a developed India. Stating that quality education, research, and character building are essential for the nation’s progress he asked educational institutions to go beyond preparing students for careers and focus on creating responsible citizens for democracy and society.The Vice President highlighted the growing achievements of women in higher education, describing it as a welcome transformation and a reflection of Nari Shakti. He noted that providing women with the right education and opportunities enables them to stand on their own feet, which constitutes true empowerment.Referring to Assam’s development trajectory, Radhakrishnan said that over the last five years, Assam’s economy has expanded by 45%, with per capita income rising by 54% from 2021-22 to 2024-25. Emphasizing Prime Minister’s vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the Vice President said the inclusive development of every state and region, particularly the North East, is essential to achieving this goal.The Vice President is on a two-day visit to Assam starting today. This afternoon, Shri Radhakrishnan will attend the Convocation Ceremony of Srimanta Sankaradeva University of Health Sciences at Jyoti-Bishnu Antarjatik Kala Mandir, Guwahati.

. In Indonesia, more than 1.5 lakh passengers were left stranded after a volcanic eruption forced authorities to temporarily suspend operations at eight airports.Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said 712 flights have so far been affected, and urged airlines to consider diverting flights to alternative airports. The Transport Ministry said the disruption has mainly affected flights to and from Singapore, along with other international routes, including Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur. Purwagandhi also called on airlines to expedite ticket refunds for passengers affected by cancellations.Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport was the first to suspend operations this morning after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau was detected in the airspace near the airport. According to Indonesia’s meteorological agency, BMKG, volcanic ash reached altitudes of up to twenty thousand feet over Java on east of the volcano, and as high as fifty thousand feet west of the volcano on the Sumatra side. Authorities said the volcano began erupting late Friday night, triggering continuous seismic activity, lava fountains and loud booming sounds across surrounding areas. Two further eruptions were recorded early this morning.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 0.4 per cent down at 95 US dollars and 10 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.6 per cent lower at 90 US dollars and 76 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. In badminton, India’s ace shuttler Kidambi Srikanth will take on Hong Kong’s Lee Cheuk Yiu in the Men’s Singles Quarterfinals at the China Masters Super 750 in Shenzhen today. Srikanth defeated world No. 9 Victor Lai of Canada, 21-18, 21-19, yesterday.India’s top Men’s Doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty progressed to the quarterfinals. They overcame a mid-match wobble to beat French brothers Christo and Toma Junior Popov 21-15, 22-24, and 21-9. However, in Women’s Singles, teenager Tanvi Sharma bowed out in the Round of 16 after a three-game loss to Japan’s Tomoka Miyazak. Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto were also eliminated from Mixed Doubles.

. The 5th Sohra International Half Marathon 2026 was successfully held today, bringing together regional, national, and international athletes to Meghalaya.The event was organised by the Meghalaya State Olympics Association (MSOA) in collaboration with the Directorate of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Meghalaya, Meghalaya Athletics Association and an official recognised by the Athletics Federation of India (AFI).The 2026 edition saw the registration of 11,672 runners across all categories. Participation included international athletes and runners from other states as well.In his keynote address,Wailadmiki Shylla, Minister, Department of Sports and YouthAffairs, Government of Meghalaya highlighted the event’s remarkable evolution from a modest starting field of 750 runners to nearly 12,000 participants.Welcoming athletes representing almost 24 states across the country, Shylla emphasized the marathon’s  widespread socio-economic impact, which directly benefits local homestay operators, transport providers, and farmers, while establishing Sohra as a top-tier sporting destination beyond its traditional fame for rainand waterfalls.Sukant Suki Singh, the first Indian to Complete three 200-Mile Ultramarathons, praisedMeghalaya’s exceptional sports infrastructure and natural beauty, identifying the state as the future sporting capital of India.He specifically commended Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangmafor completely transforming the region’s sports landscape and actively nurturing athletic talent from a young age.The Sohra Half Marathon witnessed strong performances across all its competitive categories, with Satish Kumar Verma emerging winner in the Elite Men’s 21 km category with a timing of 1:03:04, and Tejaswini Narendra Lambkane claiming the Elite Women’s title in 1:15:20.

. In Women’s Cricket, India will take on arch-rivals Pakistan in the final Group A clash of the T20 Asia Cup at the Dubai International Stadium tonight. The match will begin at 8 PM Indian Standard Time.India have already secured a place in the semi-finals after recording convincing victories over Thailand and Hong Kong in their previous two matches.The Indian team will now look to maintain its winning run and finish the group stage with a perfect record.Pakistan, meanwhile, have played just one match. They began their campaign with a win over Thailand.The team currently has two points in Group A and needs just one more point from its remaining two matches to qualify for the semi-finals. Their last league game is against Hong Kong.Last night, Hosts United Arab Emirates (UAE) defeated Indonesia by six wickets at the Dubai International Stadium. Chasing a target of 72 runs, the UAE overhauled the score, posting 75 for the loss of four wickets in 13.1 overs.Earlier, put in to bat, Indonesia were bowled out for 71 in 19.4 overs.

. In football, India qualified for the AFC U20 Asian Cup main tournament for the first time in 20 years, after a 3-nil win over Bangladesh in their final qualifying match in Tashkent yesterday.In their final Group B qualifier, Danny Meitei Laishram opened the scoring in the 25th minute, before Vishal Yadav doubled India’s lead with an acrobatic finish on the hour mark. Substitute Md Arbash made it 3-nil in the 79th minute.The victory, India’s second in the qualifiers, took them to six points from three matches. India then waited for the result of the Syria-Uzbekistan match.Uzbekistan’s 3-nil win over Syria confirmed India’s qualification as one of the seven best runners-up across the eight groups. India last featured in the AFC U20 Asian Cup in 2006. Uzbekistan topped Group B with nine points, while Syria finished third with three points. Bangladesh, who lost all three matches, were relegated to the Development Phase.The AFC U20 Asian Cup will be held in China from 24th March to 10th April, next year.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah today outlined a three-year roadmap to make India drug-free by 2029, calling for a coordinated national campaign against narcotics. Mr Shah was addressing a press conference in Goa during his three-day visit to the state.He said the government has strengthened enforcement, intelligence-sharing, financial investigations and rehabilitation measures since 2019. More than 1.19 crore kilograms of drugs, valued at about one lakh 89 thousand crore rupees, were seized between 2014 and 2024, while over 48.66 lakh kilograms were destroyed.Mr Shah said the roadmap is based on four pillars – intelligence- and operations-based enforcement, control of precursor and synthetic drugs, demand and harm reduction, and capacity building and coordination.The government has set a target of dismantling 100 international and inter-state drug networks, bringing 100 narcotics-related fugitives to India and destroying 100 clandestine drug laboratories over the next three years.The campaign will reach 50 crore citizens and create one lakh ‘Nasha Mukt Mitras’. The number of de-addiction centres will be increased to 1,751.Mr Shah said Goa has an Anti-Narcotics Task Force and urged public and media support for the campaign.

. US defence giant GE Aerospace has delivered a fresh batch of three F404-IN20 engines to Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), providing a crucial boost to the country’s domestic Tejas Mk1A fighter jet programme. The F404 engines are being supplied under a 2021 contract between HAL and GE Aerospace for 99 power plants intended to equip the initial fleet of Tejas Mk1A jets. The programme has grappled with years of delivery bottlenecks stemming from international supply chain constraints, which previously left completed airframes waiting on engine integration.

. India’s services sector strengthened in August, supported by resilient export demand, while employment reached a 15-month high. The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) Business Activity Index rose to 54.1 in August, up from 53.3 in July. Despite the acceleration, the overall pace of expansion remained the second-weakest since March 2022, and stayed marginally below the long-run average of 54.5.The report noted that new business gained momentum in August due to stronger customer demand and marketing initiatives. However, the growth rate in sales was the second-slowest in nearly four-and-a-half-years, impacted by challenging market conditions and softer client appetite in selected services.According to the latest data compiled by S&P Global, input cost inflation edged up slightly last month due to higher spending on digital platforms, electricity, inputs, labour, marketing and regulatory requirements.Meanwhile, the HSBC India Composite PMI Output Index stood at 54.3 in August, unchanged from July, as faster growth in services offset a slowdown in manufacturing.

. At the China Masters badminton, Indian men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty entered their fourth-straight China Masters semifinal after beating Denmark’s Kim Astrup and Anders Skaarup Rasmussen 21-13, 16-21, 21-18 in Shenzhen this evening.The Indian pair defeated France’s Toma Junior Popov and Christo Popov 21-17, 22-24, 21-9, last night, to make it to the quarterfinal.In men’s singles Kidambi Srikanth’s campaign at the China Masters, ended after losing 16-21, 16-21 to Lee Cheuk Yiu of Hong Kong in the quarterfinals in Shenzhen today.Earlier, India’s women’s singles campaign came to an end yesterday after Tanvi Sharma lost 21-17, 18-21, 21-16 against Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki.

. The seven core OPEC+ countries –  Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman met virtually yesterday to review global market conditions and outlook. They decided to keep its oil output policy unchanged for ‌October amid global uncertainty.The decision comes after OPEC+ increased production by around 188-thousand barrels per day for September, completing the rollback of a voluntary production cut of around 1.65 million barrels per day that had been introduced in 2023.The meeting comes against the backdrop of continuing disruptions to oil exports, including those linked to the conflict involving Iran and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz. These disruptions have limited the impact of OPEC+ production decisions on global oil supplies and prices. It is worth noting that the United Arab Emirates (UAE) had left the alliance in May this year, citing national interest and commitment to contributing effectively to meeting the market’s pressing needs.OPEC+ is expected to meet again in October to review market conditions and production levels.

. Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav arrived in Dubai yesterday on a 3-day visit to UAE. He will be participating in the Annual Investment Meeting (AIM) Congress in Dubai and will engage with investors, pitching Madhya Pradesh as an attractive investment destination.Outlining the objective of the visit, he said that the goal is to attract investment in every sector, including logistics, mining, agriculture, food processing, textiles and artificial intelligence, to boost trade and create new employment opportunities for the youth of the state.Expressing confidence that investors will become partners in Madhya Pradesh’s journey of development, the Chief Minister said that that more than 900 outdated laws were abolished, along with several policies to simplify procedures and reduce delays. This, he said, has led to faster project implementation.Dr. Mohan Yadav met President of the Arab Parliament, Mohammed Ahmed Al Yammahi, and invited him and the members of the Arab Parliament to participate and invest in Global Investment Summit that the state is scheduled to host early next year.The Chief Minister also inaugurated a special exhibition showcasing Madhya Pradesh’s ‘One District One Product’ initiative, giving the state’s unique local products a platform to reach global markets and connect with international buyers, an important step in taking these products ‘from local to global’. The products showcased included Bell Metal Craft of Betul, Chanderi handlooms from Ashoknagar, Batik dyeing art from Ujjain, Maheshwari Saree from Khargone and Gwalior Carpet, among others.Dr. Mohan Yadav said that an economy is built on the strong foundations of products from various districts and that Madhya Pradesh offers a wide variety of local products.Later in the evening, he also participated in “Tycoons by AIM Congress” – a niche gathering of influential policymakers, investment leaders, sovereign wealth executives, unicorn founders and entrepreneurs.Dr. Mohan Yadav is leading a Madhya Pradesh delegation to the AIM Congress, being held in Dubai from 7th to 9th September 2026. The Chief Minister will inaugurate the Madhya Pradesh Pavilion and address an investment session at this event on Monday. He will also meet representatives of major business groups in Dubai and Sharjah to present Madhya Pradesh’s industrial and tourism potential to global investors.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called upon the automotive industry to deepen localisation, expand exports and prepare to serve global markets. The Minister was addressing the 66th Society of Indian Automobile Manufactures-SIAM Annual Convention in New Delhi yesterday. He urged the industry to seize the opportunities emerging from India’s expanding trade partnerships, growing domestic market and global shifts in manufacturing.Mr Goyal said the automotive sector would be one of the most important drivers of India’s growth story in the years to come. He said the industry had demonstrated strong growth and that rising incomes and aspirations offered considerable scope for this growth to continue. The Commerce and Industry Minister said the AI will help the automotive industry become more efficient, competitive and customer-friendly. He added that the government is ready to support industry with critical minerals, technology, plug-and-play infrastructure and industrial parks.

. Union Minister of State for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr Jitendra Singh, has called for stronger collaboration between government research institutions, industry and start-ups.He said collaborations are required to accelerate innovation and ensure that scientific research reaches the market and benefits citizens. Addressing the inaugural session of the two-day RISE Conclave in Kolkata today, Dr Singh said the Government has opened up several strategic scientific sectors, including space and atomic energy, for greater private-sector participation. Dr Jitendra Singh said a stronger research-to-market ecosystem will contribute to technological self-reliance and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.Various projects including launching of new website of CSIR have been initiated by Shri Jitendra Singh and MoUs have been exchanged between private scientific organisations and CSIR in presence of the Minister today.The RISE Conclave – Research, Industry and Start-up Entrepreneurship – focuses on four key areas: Minerals, Medicine, Materials and Machines. It aims to strengthen research-industry linkages, promote technology transfer and nurture scientific entrepreneurship.The conclave is jointly organised by four CSIR laboratories – CSIR-IICB, CSIR-CGCRI, CSIR-CMERI and CSIR-IMMT. Representatives from IITs, research institutions, industry and start-ups are participating.The two-day conclave will conclude tomorrow.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that over the past several years, the relationship between India and France has reached new heights. He said, together with President Macron, both countries are building a Special Global Strategic Partnership.Speaking during inauguration of Swaminarayan Hindu Mandir in Paris through video conferencing, Mr Modi said, From technology, AI and defence to space and climate action, both nations are moving forward together with new momentum and renewed energy. He said, both sides also celebrating this year as the India-France Year of Innovation.The Prime Minister said, the India-France Strategic Partnership is special because it rests upon the strong foundation of the longstanding cultural and political connections. He said, history bears witness to the sacrifices of Indian soldiers in France, a history that continues to live in the collective memory and hearts.Mr Modi said, those interested in languages also know the important role French scholars have played in promoting and popularising Sanskrit. He said, the writings of Romain Rolland on Ramakrishna Paramahansa and Swami Vivekananda brought both societies even closer together. The Prime Minister said, from Paris to the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in Puducherry, The Mother’s spiritual journey inspired countless Indian and French seekers. He said, decades ago, Srila Prabhupada Swami also came to France and through ISKCON, he opened a new chapter in the spiritual relationship between India and France.Mr Modi said, today, yoga has also become an important medium of people-to-people connection between India and France. He said, the images from International Yoga Day in front of the Eiffel Tower are a wonderful example of the popularity of yoga in France. He added that now, through the magnificent BAPS Swaminarayan temple, a new chapter is being added to the India-France deep cultural relationship.The Prime Minister said, these days, there is much discussion about the possibilities of India-France joint ventures. He said, the Swaminarayan Temple has added a new dimension to this possibility as well. He added that this temple is Made in India and Built in France. Mr Modi said, a significant portion of the stone used in the temple was carved in India. He said, India’s ancient craftsmanship and talent have now come together with modern engineering in France.The Prime Minister hoped that this temple will stand for centuries as a symbol of cooperation and the immense possibilities that exist between India and France. He said, Swaminarayan temples have always been centres not only of devotion but also of service. Mr Modi expressed confidence that the cultural and spiritual messages that emanate from the temple will benefit people across Europe. He said, the temple will not only enrich the diversity of France, but will also bring renewed energy to the cultural relationship between India and France.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. The Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has received seven awards at the Federation of Indian Publishers (FIP) Awards for Excellence in Book Production, 2026. The Division’s journals, books and reference publications in Hindi, English and Urdu have been recognised in various categories.Director General, Publications Division, Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia said that the books and journals published by the Division play an important role in bringing diverse and valuable content related to national development, literature, culture, art and contemporary issues to readers. He said, the seven awards received by the Publications Division are a testament to the collective hard work, dedication and excellence of its officers and personnel.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. The Ministry of External Affairs responded to the UN General Assembly resolution on equal-area world map. Spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal said that India has voted in favour of the United Nations General Assembly resolution on equal-area cartographic representation.Mr Jaiswal further added that India’s sovereign territory, including the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, must be depicted in accordance with India’s official map. He also clarified that any inaccurate or misleading depiction is unacceptable. He said the government’s position on India’s sovereignty and territorial integrity is clear, consistent and non-negotiable.Mr Jaiswal said that the UN General Assembly adopted a resolution titled “Correct the Map Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World’s Regions, Particularly Africa” on 4th of this month. He said, the purpose of this is to encourage the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses.The Spokesperson said, India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation of vote stressing on the underlying principle of promoting equal – area cartographic representation. He highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection, or depiction of national boundaries.

. On the eve of Raksha Bandhan, President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to people. The President said that the festival of Raksha Bandhan has been an integral part of country’s culture and tradition since ancient times. She said that rakhi thread, tied around the wrist with faith, is regarded as a sacred bond of protection, known as Raksha Bandhan.The President  said that in many shlokas and mantras, Rakshe, Ma Chala, Ma Chala can be found which expresses the imploration that may this bond of protection continue forever. President Murmu urged every citizen to take a pledge to strengthen the bonds amongst families and communities, marching forward with this spirit towards a Viksit Bharat.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to countrymen on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. In his message, Mr Birla said festival that celebrates the mutual love, affection, and trust between brothers and sisters. He noted that the festival symbolizes of India’s rich culture, family values, and the unbreakable bonds of affection and belonging.

. The government has extended the last date for submission of applications by selected meritorious students for National Means cum Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) for 2026-27 to 30th September this year. The NMMSS is implemented through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP). Following the extension, the last date for Level-1 verification at the Institute Nodal Officer is 15th October while the last date for Level-2 verification with the District Nodal Officer is 31st October.The National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme awards scholarships to meritorious students from economically weaker sections to prevent drop-out of students after elementary level that is Class eight and encourage them to complete their school education up to higher secondary level that is Class 12. The scholarship amount is 12 thousand rupees per annum per student.The Scheme provides one lakh fresh scholarships every year for Class 9 students who clear the qualifying exam for the scholarship conducted by the State and UT governments. The scholarship is continued through renewal mode from Classes 10 to 12 based on the student’s academic performance. The scheme is applicable only to students studying in State Government, Government-aided and local body schools.The eligibility parameters for availing the scholarship include parental income of not more than 3.50 lakh rupees per annum, a minimum of 55 per cent marks or equivalent grade in the Class 8 examination for appearing in the selection test for award of scholarship. The government has advised all the eligible students to complete their scholarship applications on the National Scholarship Portal within the extended timeline.

. At least 25 people were killed in a bus accident in the African island nation of Cape Verde. According to local media and officials, the accident occurred yesterday on the Campanas de Cima route, a mountainous area on Fogo Island, and involved a passenger bus. Several other people were also injured in the incident. In a social media post, Cape Verdean President Jose Maria Pereira Neves described the accident as a great catastrophe.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has said that the country today stands as an important place of transformation and renewed confidence, showcasing the results of collective determination and efforts. The Vice President said this after releasing a book titled Sankalp Se Siddhi ka Modi Yug written by Rajya Sabha MP Ghanshyam Tiwari. He said that whether it is advancing technology, building modern infrastructure, and strengthening national unity and promoting women-led development, education is the tool for empowerment. Mr Radhakrishnan also highlighted the contributions of the country’s youth, women, farmers, workers, and every citizen for their involvement in building a stronger and prosperous nation. He also underlined that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is the only leader in the world to provide free Covid-19 vaccines not only to 140 crore Indian people but also to hundred more countries.Speaking about the book, the Vice President said that through the publication, the author seeks to bring together many aspects of country’s larger narratives, reviving pride in cultural heritage and enhancing the country’s voice at the global stage. He added that the book reflects the journey of the nation and encourages everyone and boosts their enthusiasm.

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has issued a clarification on reports circulating in the media regarding speculations and misinformation that there is an attempt to privatise ISRO or reduce its role. In a social media post, ISRO said that it will neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished. It added that participation of the private sector in space is aimed at enabling ISRO to focus even more strongly on the next generation of India’s space programme, while industry scales up mature technologies and capabilities.ISRO said the space-sector reforms aim to create a larger, stronger and globally competitive Indian space ecosystem. It said the reforms should therefore be seen as ecosystem expansion and capability multiplication, rather than privatisation.Noting the growth in India’s industrial and technological capabilities, ISRO said that mature and scalable activities can increasingly be undertaken by Indian industry. This would enable large-scale production, commercialisation, innovation and access to global markets, while allowing ISRO’s scientific and technical manpower to concentrate on advanced research, next-generation technologies and complex national missions.ISRO said this approach will allow it to devote more resources and scientific manpower to the next generation of technologies and missions, while the wider ecosystem provides the investment, manufacturing capacity and scale required by an expanding national space programme.

. Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda spoke with Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and took stock of the situation following the building collapse in Satya Niketan area of New Delhi today. Mr Nadda assured all possible support from the Ministry of Health. He also directed the Director of AIIMS and Central Government hospitals to provide all possible medical support and assistance.

. In Badminton, Indian men’s doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will take on the Malaysian duo of Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong in the semi-final of the China Masters in Shenzhen today.The Indian pair defeated Denmark’s Kim Astrup and Anders Skaarup Rasmussen 21-13, 16-21, 21-18 in the quarter-final yesterday. With the victory, Satwik and Chirag reached the semi-finals of the China Masters for the fourth consecutive time.On the other hand their Malaysian opponents, Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong, pulled off a major upset by defeating Indonesia’s world No. 7 pair, Sabar Karyaman Gutama and Moh Reza Pahlevi Isfahani, 21-17, 16-21, 21-19.The victory earned them their first-ever Super 750 semi-final appearance.Meanwhile, India’s campaign in the singles events came to an end as Kidambi Srikanth lost to Hong Kong’s Lee Cheuk Yiu in the Men’s Singles quarter-final. In Women’s Singles, Tanvi Sharma went down against Japan’s Tomoka Miyazaki.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and parts of North East India for today. Met Department predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu today.Similar weather conditions are also expected over Puducherry, Karaikal, Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh, East Rajasthan and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Weather Agency has also predicted a spell of light rainfall at a few places in Delhi today.

. At the Pickleball World Cup 2026, India remained unbeaten on the opening day of the Team Event in Da Nang, Vietnam. The tournament is being held till the 6th of this month. This marks the end of the league stage, where a dominant India defeated Antigua and Barbuda, Israel and the Czech Republic. The Indian Pro squad recorded dominant victories over Antigua and Barbuda and Israel, winning both ties 6-0. India then defeated the Czech Republic 5-1 to top the league stage.The team will now face Portugal in the Round of 32. India’s Senior squad also had a strong start, defeating Germany and Nepal 4-0 each to advance to the Round of 32. India has bagged a total of 37 medals so far in the tournament, including six gold, 16 silver and 15 bronze. Unbeaten through the team league stage, India is currently at the 4th spot in the medal tally.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi rose nearly 0.3 per cent while Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 0.2 per cent. In European markets, Germany’s DAX was trading almost flat, and London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.4 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices rebounded today, snapping a four-session losing streak. The Sensex climbed 363 points or half a per cent to close at 76,515, while the Nifty added 24 points or 0.1 per cent to settle at 23,898. However, in the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell 0.2 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index gained 0.2 per cent.Earlier, the markets opened with a gap-up amid positive global cues. Both benchmark indices remained in the green throughout the session, trading within a narrow range. However, following the closing auction session, the indices pared some of their gains.In the Sensex pack, 20 out of 30 companies logged gains. Among the top movers, Tata Steel jumped 2.9 per cent, Reliance gained 1.6 per cent and Bajaj Finance advanced one and a half per cent. In contrast, Bharti Airtel as well as HCL Tech declined 1.2 per cent, Eternal dropped 1.1 per cent and Asian Paints lost half a per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 16 out of 28 sectors edged upward. Among the top performers, Housing Finance, Metal, Telecommunication and Insurance rose 1.4 per cent, Commodities and Financial Services gained 0.6 per cent and Private Banks Index added half a per cent. In contrast, Realty and Capital Goods declined 0.7 per cent, Healthcare fell half a per cent and Hospitals lost 0.4 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2388 companies advanced, 1991 declined and 239 remained unchanged.

. India’s foreign exchange reserves surged by 11.4 billion US dollars to a record high of 740.8 billion dollars during the week ended 28th of last month.According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 9.3 billion US dollars to 600.6 billion dollars during the week. Gold reserves added 2.1 billion dollars to 116.4 billion dollars.However, Special Drawing Rights declined by 43 million dollars to 18.8 billion dollars. Country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped 11 million dollars to 4.9 billion dollars.

. The Indian Air Force (IAF) Sarang Helicopter Display Team has reached Egypt to participate in the 2nd edition of the EI Alamein International Airshow. The Air Show is scheduled to be held from 08th to 10th of this month at EI Alamein International Airport.The Ministry of Defence said that the team will showcase precision, professionalism and flying skills through a series of meticulously choreographed displays. The Ministry added that this will mark another significant milestone in international engagements by the IAF reflecting growing defence and diplomatic ties between India and Egypt.The Ministry further stated that Sarang team will be flying the indigenously designed and manufactured Advanced Light Helicopter Dhruv.

. Tensions between Iran and the United States continue to escalate, with both sides carrying out strikes against each other amid growing military confrontation in the region. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) today said that its aerospace forces had targeted a US aircraft carrier and a destroyer with several ballistic missiles.The IRGC claimed the vessels had harassed Iranian ships and participated in a naval blockade against Iran. It warned that if the hostile and aggressive actions continue, the US government should expect a formidable response from Iran’s armed forces.The escalation follows overnight strikes by the IRGC Navy, which said it had targeted three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels elsewhere. Iran described the attacks as retaliation for US strikes on Iranian tankers earlier in the day. Meanwhile, US Central Command yesterday said that US forces had struck three Iranian crude-oil carriers. The US military said the strikes came after the IRGC launched ballistic missiles toward two US Navy warships patrolling waters in the region.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. Customs officials have seized 134 silver coins with apparent archaeological significance among 484 silver coins and one gold coin from two passengers arriving from Doha at the Indira Gandhi International Airport.According to an official statement, Air Customs officers intercepted the two passengers after they arrived on September 2. An examination of their baggage led to the recovery and seizure of 20.883 kilograms of gold and silver coins, collectively valued at 47.16 lakh rupees in tariff value, for attempted clearance without declaration.The seized goods comprised 484 silver coins and one gold coin. Of the silver coins recovered, 134 were reported to have apparent archaeological significance by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). The goods were seized under Section 110 of the Customs Act, 1962. It said further investigation is underway.

. The US trade deficit in goods and services surged 24.4 per cent in July, to 88.6 billion US dollars. That is higher than the upwardly revised figure of 71.2 billion US dollars recorded in June, according to data from the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) and the US Census Bureau. The increase came as US imports rose, while exports declined. Exports fell 2.1 per cent to 310.7 billion US dollars, while imports climbed 2.8 per cent to 399.3 billion US dollars.The US also recorded a five-billion-dollar goods trade deficit with India in July. The largest US goods trade deficit was with Mexico, at 27.5 billion US dollars, followed by Vietnam, Taiwan, China, South Korea and the European Union. The services sector provided a relatively small offset to the widening goods deficit. Services exports declined by 0.4 billion billion US dollars to 109.7 billion, while services imports fell by 0.6 billion US dollars to 78.7 billion.

. In Shooting, the Indian team will be attending its final training camp ahead of the Asian Games 2026 starting later this month in Japan. The camp begins at the Madhya Pradesh State Shooting Academy in Bhopal today.A total of 18 shooters, including nine men and nine women, will be taking part in the camp. The squad includes top shooters such as Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh, and Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar.Expert coaches will be training the shooters in rifle and pistol events. The camp will be focusing on shooting skills, fitness, recovery, and mental strength. The shooters will also be training at modern 10, 25, and 50-metre ranges.A special training camp was held in Bhopal last month as well. The Indian shooting team will leave for the Asian Games after the camp concludes on 14th September.

. In Badminton, Indian pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty clinched the men’s doubles title at the China Masters in Shenzhen today. The Indian duo defeated China’s He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu 11-21, 21-13, 21-17 in the summit clash to secured India’s first-ever title at the China Masters.The victory marks the duo’s second title of the season. They had earlier won the Singapore Open Super 750 and finished runners-up at the Thailand Open Super 500. Satwik and Chirag booked their place in the final after defeating Malaysia’s Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong 21-15, 18-21, 21-11 in the semifinals. The Indian duo had finished runners-up at the China Masters in 2023 and 2025 and reached the semifinals in 2024.

. The Goa Government will launch the ‘Goa Ujjwala Scheme’ on September 5, providing financial assistance equivalent to the cost of three domestic LPG cylinders every year to eligible household LPG and PNG consumers. Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant said ₹3,000 will be directly transferred into beneficiaries’ bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).The Civil Supplies Department has made a provision of ₹100 crore for the scheme. There is no income criterion for availing the benefit. However, only one domestic gas connection per family will be eligible. Existing Griha Aadhar and Deen Dayal Social Security Scheme beneficiaries can apply by submitting the scheme application and bank passbook. A separate application will be available for open-category beneficiaries. Applications will be available at panchayat and municipal offices. The first instalment is expected to be credited to beneficiaries’ bank accounts on September 9 or 10.

. In Women’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by seven wickets in the Women’s Asia Cup T20 match in Dubai. Pakistan were bowled out for just 55 in 18.1 overs, their lowest-ever total in T20 Internationals.Young spinners Shree Charani and Prema Rawat took three wickets each, while Deepti Sharma claimed two. India chased down the target in 8.4 overs, with captain Harmanpreet Kaur remaining unbeaten on 18. The match also marked Harmanpreet’s 150th T20 International as India’s captain, making her the first international captain, male or female, to reach the milestone.Pakistan started confidently at 27 without loss but lost six wickets for just nine runs as India’s spinners took complete control. Charani returned figures of three for seven, while Rawat took three for nine. India’s bowlers bowled 78 dot balls in Pakistan’s innings and never allowed the opposition to recover. India have now won seven of the eight T20 Asia Cup meetings against Pakistan.
